verdicts.why: On gloss — a thing taken up so often that nothing in it can still surprise is overfamiliarity through overuse, and the mileage-not-damage image serves that figurative sense exactly as the threadbare and shopworn notes do — with no distribution or provenance claim, a negative lightest-tier charge the note itself calls a lighter charge, both comparatives agreeing with the threadbare ('harsher than well-worn') and shopworn ('grubbier than well-worn') notes, and a 'mileage' position (exhausted by use) distinct from commonplace's ordinariness, timeworn's age and stock's category, with no superlative left to collide.

On gloss — a settled mind stirred into agitation is the worry-and-anxiety end of 'causing distress or worry or anxiety' — with no distribution or provenance claim, a negative charge, and comparatives that check against the family (lighter than disturbing's -2, 'more momentary' than a note that says disturbing 'goes on unsettling'); 'momentary' is the weakest clause because the word states no duration, but as a comparative against a neighbour that claims persistence it shades the sense rather than narrowing it, and the composure image it shares with disturbing is differentiated by weight, not simply re-claimed.
